items.title: The Braille Reader Who Chose a Different Subscription
items.pitch: Help a child complete real Braille instruction. A later adult may choose an available audio subscription instead of continuing a paid printed series, keeping the old reading skill while changing who gets the next order.

present_hook.what_you_notice: An unfinished accessible-reading enrollment sits beside a real unpaid resource estimate.

clues.line: The course in {year} never cleared its actual materials and instruction gap.

window.notes: C is A actual parent, direction C parent to A, and gives necessary guardian consent. A is an actual blind child freely wanting suitable Braille literacy instruction, with independently established reading needs and a genuine course/resource gap. B owns a real appropriately qualified accessible-format publishing operation. Baseline no completed course or paid A subscription. No later reading preference is predetermined.

interventions.how_it_looks: Cover the actual shortfall through the properly supervised instruction account.

ripples.headline: A Child Completes Suitable Braille Instruction
ripples.body: Actual qualified instruction and attendance produce only the assessed real learning. No change in vision or professional qualification is implied.

ripples.headline: An Adult Reader Receives a Real Authorized Braille Series
ripples.body: The now-adult reader freely pays an affordable actual subscription and receives the genuinely available authorized editions under its real terms.

ripples.headline: A Reader Freely Changes a Real Subscription Format
ripples.body: The reader lawfully ends the actual print subscription and takes an independently available accessible audio service using real funds and suitable equipment. Earlier owned copies and actual skills are not erased.

fails.headline: The Course Does Not Become Completed Instruction
fails.body: The supervised gift follows actual fee and refund terms. No literacy result, paid order or later preference is created.

present_day.best: If the chain occurred and the arrangements remain current in {now}, permitted household records show the actual format change, surviving owned print copies and real audio entitlement/equipment. Describe retained Braille skill only from current actual assessment.
present_day.worst: No course dictates a future preference. Actual access, skills, editions, devices and subscriptions require their own real facts.
present_day.twist: The reader gains a freely chosen real format and gives up the next print-series deliveries within the actual budget. The original publisher loses that genuine continuing customer order without losing ownership of its own work or the reader losing a right to choose.

npc_lines_after.line: The old copies were paid for. The new orders stopped.

items.title: The Fishing Derby That Ended with Refunds
items.pitch: Introduce a real organizer to a willing bait-shop sponsor. A durable river event may later honor its refund promise during an actual closure, returning entry money while leaving its organizer with a paid printing bill.

present_hook.what_you_notice: An unused derby poster has a blank sponsor line and no completed first-event record.

clues.line: The proposal in {year} needed a willing sponsor, actual permissions and real operating funds.

window.notes: A is an actual willing competent prospective organizer. B owns the real bait shop and genuinely wants to consider the proposal. They are unrelated strangers. Bind an actual suitable permitted river site, available lawful event resources and real existing willing adult participants. Baseline no completed derby or sponsorship. No fish, catch, unsafe water or closure is presumed.

interventions.how_it_looks: Arrange a mutually wanted meeting about the genuine event and sponsorship proposal.

ripples.headline: A River Fishing Derby Completes Its First Lawful Event
ripples.body: Actual willing participants complete the funded permitted program under its real rules. Only genuine recorded catches and results count.

ripples.headline: A Continuing Derby Adopts a Funded Refund Promise
ripples.body: The actual current organizers freely adopt lawful cancellation terms and hold genuine entry/refund funds under the agreed controls. No weather or future turnout is guaranteed.

ripples.headline: A Genuine River Closure Brings Actual Entry Refunds
ripples.body: An independently real applicable closure prevents the genuine scheduled event. Organizers complete the required lawful cancellation and refund actual paid entries; genuinely sunk printing costs remain paid.

fails.headline: The First Derby Does Not Complete
fails.body: A meeting creates no sponsor payment, entrant, catch or event. Actual preliminary agreements and deposits follow their real terms.

present_day.best: If the chain occurred and the records survive in {now}, the event account shows the actual closure, completed valid refunds and the genuine nonrefundable printing expense of {A}. Show a canceled poster only if the actual printed asset survives.
present_day.worst: No event creates a fish or forces a dangerous river condition. Every actual permit, closure, refund and later event follows its own facts.
present_day.twist: Entrants recover real money under their actual rights. The organizer bears the actual personally paid unrecoverable printing cost and loses that planned occasion, even though the promise was kept.

npc_lines_after.line: The entry money went back. The printer had already been paid.

items.title: The Parlor Menu That Got Smaller So a Job Could Stay
items.pitch: Invest in the real freezer plan of a parlor. A larger menu may support a paid job, then shrink under actual costs so that worker stays while a regular customer loses a favorite order.

present_hook.what_you_notice: A parlor archive contains an uncompleted freezer proposal and a real menu already offering a labor-intensive specialty.

clues.line: The equipment plan in {year} had a real funding gap; its proposed larger menu was never completed.

window.notes: A owns the actual lawful parlor and a genuine costed freezer/menu plan. B is an actual willing potential worker, not assumed qualified. C is an actual repeat customer with a documented preference for the genuine existing labor-intensive specialty. Bind real recipes, stock controls and equipment shortfall. Baseline no completed expansion or new hire; future costs and orders are not promised.

interventions.how_it_looks: Fund the actual freezer-plan shortfall through the business account of the owner.

ripples.headline: A Parlor Completes a Funded Freezer and Menu Plan
ripples.body: Actual equipment and qualified validated production make the genuine expanded menu available. No customer, revenue or health outcome is invented.

ripples.headline: A Parlor Fills an Actual Paid Preparation Vacancy
ripples.body: The operating parlor hires the genuinely qualified willing adult into a real funded lawful role. Pay accrues only for actual work.

ripples.headline: A Parlor Cuts Real Menu Items and Keeps a Funded Job
ripples.body: Under actual independently recorded costs and a viable real plan, the owner removes specified labor-intensive items while retaining the existing paid role. A genuine affected customer order is lawfully canceled and settled.

fails.headline: The Freezer Plan Does Not Complete
fails.body: The investment follows actual contracts and accounts. No equipment, menu, hire or later cut is supplied.

present_day.best: If the chain occurred and the decision remains current in {now}, the real menu omits the recorded specialty, current employment/pay records support the retained role, and the actual canceled order of {C} and settlement are documented. Later changes remain possible.
present_day.worst: A bigger freezer guarantees no sales or job. Real staffing, recipes, costs and customer commitments retain their actual status after a failed step.
present_day.twist: The worker keeps an actual funded job while the regular customer loses an actual ordered specialty despite receiving the required settlement. The owner pays real refund and operating costs rather than receiving free payroll support.

npc_lines_after.line: I got my money back. That does not put my usual back on the board.

items.title: The Falsely Accused Candidate Who Kept the Public Receipts
items.pitch: Spread a false story about an honest candidate. A lost campaign may later lead to a real newspaper and verified civic reporting, but useful reporting will not erase the office opportunity you helped take away.

present_hook.what_you_notice: The original present has an actual mayoral record for a candidate whose real public-fund accounts show no missing money.

clues.line: The accounts from {year} were complete. A claim that the candidate took the money would be false.

window.notes: A is an actual viable willing mayoral candidate with independently verified honest management of the specified real fund and genuine writing competence. B is an existing eligible rival resident, not promised any win. Bind the actual race and authentic balanced accounts proving the proposed allegation false. Baseline A completed the original election path without this false withdrawal; no later publication, mayor or error is assumed.

interventions.how_it_looks: Knowingly repeat the false claim that the candidate took the specified public money; keep its falsity explicit in simulation records.

ripples.headline: A Candidate Freely Withdraws after a False Story Circulates
ripples.body: Under a genuine documented campaign setback, the actual candidate completes a lawful voluntary withdrawal. The allegation remains false; no public money disappeared.

ripples.headline: A Qualified Writer Opens a Funded Independent Publication
ripples.body: With actual capital, lawful resources and competent staff, the former candidate opens a genuine independent publishing operation. No readership or profit is guaranteed.

ripples.headline: Verified Public Accounts Receive a Factual Correction
ripples.body: The publication completes a genuine evidence-based correction of a real procedural account error during an actual mayoral tenure. Distinct modeled responses affect the publisher and standing of the officeholder; the error is not labeled a crime.

fails.headline: The False Story Does Not Produce a Withdrawal
fails.body: The direct reputational harm and any actual consequences remain. No withdrawal, newspaper or verified later error is created through this failed chain.

present_day.best: If the chain occurred and the records survive in {now}, the real paper contains its supported correction alongside authentic source accounts, while the old false allegation is still identified as false. Display {B} as current mayor only if actual current terms support it.
present_day.worst: A false accusation can remain only damage. Later work, elections, accounts and publications need their own real facts; no civic benefit is owed in exchange for the harm.
present_day.twist: The former candidate gains a genuine publishing opportunity and the town gains a verified account, while an earlier real campaign opportunity was lost. The later officeholder loses modeled standing for a documented procedural error; neither correction retroactively gives the first candidate the old office.

npc_lines_after.line: The figures are printed where anyone can check them.
